newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Gulf states discuss licenses for bank branches.
newsitem.headline: Gulf states discuss licenses for bank branches.

text.p: Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) central bank governors discussed on Monday the possibility of allowing regional banks to open branches in member states, an official said.

"There are certain requirements that have to be agreed upon so that there will be a proper procedure for allowing or licensing the banks to open branches in the Gulf area," Oman Central Bank Executive President Hamoud bin Sanjour Hashem told reporters.
He was speaking after a meeting of GCC central bank governors in Manama.

The GCC -- Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Bahrain -- is a political and economic alliance. It is working to unify economic and monetary policies as part of a plan to set up a regional market.
Hashem said GCC states had not set a target date for a unified currency.
"There is no target year but there is an action plan which will be starting in 1997 to discuss this matter," he said.
All Gulf currencies -- except for Kuwait's -- are pegged to the dollar, in which their main export of crude oil is traded.
Hashem said the GCC was discussing a plan to link commercial bank automated teller machine (ATM) networks. "Implementing

this step requires measures to ensure stability of the network in GCC states before it happens, but there are serious attempts to link Kuwait's automated teller machines with the ones in Saudi Arabia," he said.

Individual banks within some GCC states have linked their ATM machines, and some banks offer ATM services at their foreign branches. But as yet there is no Gulf-wide system permitting customers to access their own accounts at any ATM.
